text_read: digest only (partial_saved excerpt of the book)
mode_evidence: Starts as deliberate visualisation ('Visualize a bright sphere', 'imagines a transparent sphere') and the text insists the goal is 'really seeing the actual inner icon (nimitta) as a bright sphere'. The sequence is the classical preliminary, learning, then counterpart sign, with a sphere that 'arises' once the mind stops. The book frames it as light kasina.
onset_evidence: Section 4.21 is written for one who has not yet seen the sphere: keep imagining a bright sphere at the centre of the body, recite 'Samma Arahang', and when the mind is still and calm a bright sphere arises. If it does not, recite 100 or 1,000 times; focus on the centre of the centre ten, a hundred or a thousand times. Prerequisite: a mind not murky with defilements, and merit from past lives. No calendar time scale; no statement that it cannot be forced, but the text says it is hard to see the sphere if the mind is murky.

conditions.posture: Upright, legs crossed, right index finger touching left thumb.
conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Eyes closed; at Base 4 roll the eyeballs gently upward under the closed lids.
conditions.duration_and_schedule: Recitation continued in all postures; 100 or 1,000 repetitions if the mind has not stopped.
conditions.prerequisites: Virtue; mind free of hindrances; merit from past lives.
conditions.other: Women begin at the left nostril, men at the right.

stages.label: preliminary sign (parikamma-nimitta)
stages.description: Imagined transparent sphere like a polished diamond, eyeball-sized, moved through seven bases.

stages.label: learning sign (uggaha-nimitta)
stages.description: A transparent sphere seen briefly; marks access concentration.

stages.label: counterpart sign (patibhaga-nimitta)
stages.description: Bright sphere stable for long periods; first jhana.

stages.label: Dhamma Sphere
stages.description: Bright sphere arises at the centre of the body (Position Seven), egg-yolk to sun size; recitation stops and attention rests on the pinpoint at its centre until radiant.

what_to_do_with_light: Stop still at the centre of the centre of the sphere; once the Dhamma Sphere arises, stop reciting, do not be overjoyed, keep concentrating on its centre, then proceed to further nested spheres.
obstacles_and_fixes: Drowsiness or other hindrance: keep the sign and recitation at the body centre until a light appears from inside, awakening the mind.
Mind not yet stopped: recite 100 or 1,000 times.
Giddiness at the counterpart sign: be mindful.
cautions: Murky mind makes the sphere hard to see.
Do not be overjoyed or excited when the sphere arises.
Never move the mind to follow the breath in and out.
interpretation: The bright sphere is the Dhamma Sphere or First Path sphere, the nucleus of the form aggregate and the first step toward paths, fruits and Nibbana; the method is framed as aloka-kasina with breath and recollection of the Buddha.
practice_summary: Sit upright and close your eyes. Imagine a transparent sphere like a polished diamond about the size of an eyeball at the nostril, and rest on the tiny clear spot at its centre while silently reciting 'Samma Arahang'. Never separate sphere and recitation. Move the sphere through seven bases: nostril, tear duct, centre of the head, palate (roll the eyes gently upward under closed lids here), throat opening, body centre in line with the navel, and a point two finger-breadths above the navel. Pause at each, reciting three times. At the last, stay put, keep imagining the sphere and recite until the mind stops. A bright sphere then arises; stop reciting and keep resting on its centre until it is brilliant.

key_passages.anchor: Staring-at-the-Sphere is to arrive at really seeing the actual inner icon (nimitta) as a bright sphere
key_passages.paraphrase: The aim is genuinely seeing the inner sign as a bright sphere, not merely thinking of it.

key_passages.anchor: first roll the eyeballs upward gently while keeping the eyelids closed
key_passages.paraphrase: At the fourth base the eyes are rolled up under closed lids, compared with a baby falling asleep.

key_passages.locator: 4.21 Method for one who has not yet seen the Dhamma Sphere, source lines 5040-5163
key_passages.anchor: When the mind becomes still and calm a bright sphere arises at the center of the body.
key_passages.paraphrase: For the person who sees nothing: keep imagining the sphere and reciting at the body centre; when the mind stills, the sphere arises.

key_passages.anchor: Then, there will slowly appear a light from inside, causing the mind to awaken, clear and fresh.
key_passages.paraphrase: Against hindrances such as drowsiness, continue sign and recitation at the body centre; a light appears from within.

key_passages.anchor: When the Dhamma Sphere arises, one must not be overjoyed or excited.
key_passages.paraphrase: On arising, stay unexcited and keep stopping at the centre.
